output.title: Body lotion: fill 250 mL, pump head, label, weigh

product.name: 250 mL body lotion bottle with pump head
product.description: White oval plastic bottles filled with thick body lotion (250 mL) and closed with a pump head, then front-labeled. Bottles are approximately 60×40 mm footprint and 170 mm tall.

steps.name: Fill
steps.does: Fill one 250 mL bottle with thick body lotion using a timed/volumetric fill (about 5 seconds per bottle).

steps.name: PlacePumpHead
steps.does: Place the pump head onto the bottle opening/neck position.

steps.name: ScrewDownPump
steps.does: Screw the pump head down to secure it (screw-down operation).

steps.name: FrontLabel
steps.does: Apply a front label to the bottle.

steps.name: WeighAndCameraCheck
steps.does: Weigh the filled-and-labeled bottle and perform camera inspection; compare against acceptance limits.

steps.name: RemoveRejects
steps.does: Remove any rejected bottles from the line.

steps.name: PackTwelvePerCase
steps.does: Pack finished, accepted bottles into cases with 12 bottles per case.

output.quality: Weighing + camera inspection finds out-of-spec units; rejected bottles are removed from the line (no further packing).
constraints: Operators only at the end of the line (earlier steps should be fully automated or enclosed).
Bottles are packed twelve to a case (case packing rate must match the line takt).
assumptions: Shift length is 8 hours as stated; target rate therefore 2400/8 = 300 finished bottles per hour.
Pump head screw-down time is consistent with line takt (exact seconds not provided).
Label application is fully automated (no operator intervention mid-line).
Weighing and camera inspection occur in-line without stopping accepted product.
Reject removal is automated (ejector) because operators are only at the end of the line.
Case dimensions/material and whether cases are erected inline are not specified; a standard slotted carton is assumed for packing twelve bottles.

questions.question: What is the exact pump head screw-down time per bottle (or max allowed takt at each station)? The owner only gave ~5 s for filling.
questions.why: This determines the line bottleneck station time so every station can fit within the takt.

questions.question: What are the acceptance limits and logic for the weigh + camera check (e.g., target fill weight/tolerance, label placement rules, pump seating visual criteria)?
questions.why: This decides how strict the inspection must be and whether rejects are deterministic at the twin level.

questions.question: What case/carton size and type do you use for “12 bottles per case” (and are cases pre-erected or erected on the line)?
questions.why: This sets the packaging stations (case erector/closer vs. simple pack) and carrier/conveyor handling.
